title: The 10 Best Cordless Rotary Hammers
subtitle: Battery-powered SDS-Plus rotary hammers for concrete and masonry, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: We ranked 10 cordless SDS-Plus best-sellers on rating, review volume, and features (vibration control, a clutch or bind-up sensor, and a battery in the box). Most name-brand hammers are sold as bare tools for people who already own the batteries. The list runs from a $77 bare tool for DEWALT packs to a $325 Milwaukee M18, and includes two complete kits under $120.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

scoring.review_age_weighting: Listings under 24 months old with at least 30 reviews have their review count multiplied by min(2, 24 / age in months, age floored at 6) before scoring; older listings are unchanged. Listing age is Amazon's Date First Available, or an estimate from the ASIN when the listing does not show it.

buyers_guide.q: Cordless rotary hammer or cordless hammer drill?
buyers_guide.a: A hammer drill rattles the bit with clutch plates, which is fine for a few small holes in brick. A rotary hammer uses a piston to strike the bit, so it drills concrete several times faster and can chip tile or mortar in hammer-only mode. If you're setting more than a handful of concrete anchors, get the rotary hammer.

buyers_guide.q: Should I buy one that matches my drill's batteries?
buyers_guide.a: Usually, yes. A bare DEWALT, Milwaukee, Makita, or Bosch hammer is the cheapest way in if you already own that brand's packs. If you don't own any, a kit like the Seesii or Dong Cheng includes batteries and a charger and costs less than most bare name-brand tools.

buyers_guide.q: How much impact energy do I need?
buyers_guide.a: About 1.2 to 1.5 J is enough for 1/4" to 3/8" anchor holes, often overhead. 2 to 2.6 J handles 1/2" to 3/4" holes and light chipping. Brands don't all measure it the same way, and some list foot-pounds instead of joules (1 ft-lb is about 1.36 J), so compare within a brand when you can.

buyers_guide.q: What's the difference between 5/8", 3/4", and 1" tools?
buyers_guide.a: That's the largest concrete hole each tool is rated for. The small 5/8" and 11/16" hammers are lighter and built for overhead anchor work. The 1" tools drill bigger holes faster and usually include a chisel mode, but they weigh more.

buyers_guide.q: Is a clutch or kickback control worth having?
buyers_guide.a: Yes. When a bit hits rebar or binds, a rotary hammer can twist hard enough to hurt your wrist. A clutch slips, and electronic systems like Milwaukee's AUTOSTOP or Bosch's kickback control cut power. On this list, the Milwaukee 2912-20, Bosch, Seesii, and ACROPOW listings state one.
Yes. Every tool here takes SDS-Plus bits and chisels, which lock in without a key. Regular round-shank bits need an adapter chuck, and SDS-Max bits are a larger size that won't fit.
